records.relevance_note: Terminal-agent paper; abstract describes compaction, memory, and tool-surface deferral to control context growth.
records.reason_included: Captures a modern terminal-agent harness explicitly calling out adaptive compaction and lazy tool discovery as context controls.

claim_snippets.claim_text: OPENDEV uses "lazy tool discovery" and "adaptive context compaction" that "progressively reduces older observations" to prevent context bloat during long-horizon terminal work.
OPENDEV employs an "automated memory system" to accumulate project-specific knowledge across sessions and uses "event-driven system reminders" to counteract instruction fade-out.

records.title: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents
records.relevance_note: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents is a paper source with details on context as tool, structured context workspace relevant to context engineering.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on context, memory, eval design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper argues append-only context maintenance or passively triggered compression heuristics can lead to "context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning" in long-running SWE agent interactions.

CAT formalizes a structured context workspace consisting of "stable task semantics", "condensed long-term memory", and "high-fidelity short-term interactions", and enables agents to proactively compress history into actionable summaries at milestones.
On SWE-Bench-Verified, the paper reports SWE-Compressor reaches a 57.6% solved rate and outperforms ReAct-based agents and static compression baselines under a bounded context budget.

records.title: Compaction (Claude API Docs)
records.relevance_note: Server/API-level compaction mechanism with explicit trigger configuration, compaction blocks, and continuation semantics.
records.reason_included: Primary vendor doc with concrete compaction trigger, pause, and continuation rules for long-running tool-using workloads.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When compaction is enabled, the API "detects" that input tokens exceed a trigger threshold, "generates a summary", creates a `compaction` block containing the summary, and continues the response with compacted context.

On subsequent requests, the API "automatically drops all message blocks prior to the `compaction` block", continuing the conversation from the summary; when a request contains a compaction block, "all content blocks before it are ignored".

`pause_after_compaction` pauses the API after generating the compaction summary and returns a message with stop reason `compaction`, allowing the client to append additional content blocks before continuing.
When streaming with compaction enabled, the compaction block streams as a single delta containing the complete summary content (no intermediate streaming).

records.title: Prompt caching (Claude API Docs)
records.relevance_note: Vendor caching doc detailing cache isolation boundaries, invalidation hierarchy, and accounting fields (reads vs writes vs post-breakpoint tokens).
records.reason_included: Concrete prompt-caching mechanics and invalidation rules that directly constrain context compilation and compaction strategies.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Starting February 5, 2026, Anthropic prompt caching switches from organization-level to workspace-level isolation for the Claude API (and Azure AI Foundry preview), isolating caches per workspace for data separation; Bedrock and Vertex maintain organization-level isolation.
Cache invalidation follows a hierarchy: `tools` → `system` → `messages`; changes at a higher level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels.

The doc defines cache accounting fields and a token breakdown where total input tokens are calculated as `cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens`, and `input_tokens` counts only tokens after the last breakpoint.

For concurrent requests, a cache entry becomes available only after the first response begins; to get cache hits for parallel requests, the doc instructs waiting for the first response before sending subsequent requests.

records.title: Prompt Caching 201
records.relevance_note: Prompt Caching 201 is a official doc source with details on exact prefix match, min cacheable prefix tokens 1024 relevant to context engineering.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on context, cost budget.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Cache hits require an exact repeated prefix; OpenAI prompt caching works automatically for prompts with 1024+ tokens, and cache hits occur in increments of 128 tokens.
Caching only works if two requests share the same prefix and land on the same machine; the optional `prompt_cache_key` parameter is described as a way to improve routing for shared prefixes.
The writeup states prompt caching applies to the key/value projections in transformer attention layers, letting inference reuse prior prefill work instead of recomputing it from scratch.
In an experiment described by the author (2300 prompts), cached requests were reported ~7% faster at 1024 tokens and ~67% faster TTFT at 150k+ tokens.

records.title: Shell + Skills + Compaction: Tips for long-running agents that do real work
records.relevance_note: OpenAI engineering post describing in-stream server-side compaction vs explicit compaction calls, plus on-demand loading of 'skills' to reduce prompt bloat.
records.reason_included: Concrete harness-level mechanisms for compiling context on demand (skills) and maintaining continuity via compaction and thread continuation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The post distinguishes server-side compaction (automatic, in-stream when context crosses a threshold) from the standalone `/responses/compact` endpoint (explicit control over when compaction happens).

Skills are described as a bundle of files with a `SKILL.md` manifest; when skills are available, the platform exposes each skill’s metadata (`name`, `description`, `path`) to the model, and the model reads `SKILL.md` only if it decides to invoke the skill.
The post claims combining container reuse, passing `previous_response_id`, and using compaction reduces restart behaviour and keeps multi-step jobs coherent as the thread grows.

records.title: GPT-5.2 Prompting Guide
records.relevance_note: Official guide describing compaction as a 'loss-aware compression pass' returning opaque encrypted items for continuation across long tool-heavy workflows.
records.reason_included: Bridges compaction mechanism with operational constraints (when to compact; prompt stability to avoid drift).

claim_snippets.claim_text: The guide states GPT-5.2 supports response compaction via `/responses/compact`, described as a "loss-aware compression pass" over prior conversation state that returns "encrypted, opaque items" preserving task-relevant information while reducing token footprint.
The guide emphasises compaction outputs are "opaque" and "designed for continuation, not inspection", and instructs treating compacted items as opaque (do not parse or depend on internals).
The guide warns to keep prompts functionally identical when resuming after compaction to avoid behaviour drift, and suggests compacting after major milestones rather than every turn.

records.reason_included: Primary schema-level source for how compaction output must be represented and carried forward in subsequent requests.

records.title: Architecting efficient context-aware multi-agent framework for production
records.relevance_note: Production-oriented context engineering writeup describing 'context as a compiled view' and handoff translation for multi-agent systems.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete context compilation/working-context assembly metaphors (sessions/memory/artifacts -> compiler pipeline -> working context) and handoff translation mechanics.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The post argues the naive pattern of appending everything into one prompt collapses under cost/latency growth, signal degradation ("lost in the middle"), and eventual window overflow.

It proposes treating context as a compiled view: sessions/memory/artifacts are the sources of structured state, flows/processors are the compiler pipeline, and the working context is the compiled view shipped to the LLM for a single invocation.

For agent handoff, the post describes an active translation: narrative casting of prior assistant messages and explicit attribution/summarisation of tool calls from other agents so the new agent can act on results without misattributing capabilities or history.

records.title: Context caching not working with Agent Engine (VertexAiSessionService drops cache_metadata) #4698
records.relevance_note: Concrete failure report showing how session persistence bugs can break context caching, forcing repeated cache creation and higher token/cost.
records.reason_included: Includes named ADK components (VertexAiSessionService, ContextCacheRequestProcessor) and a precise non-reuse failure mode tied to metadata persistence.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports `VertexAiSessionService` does not persist `cache_metadata` or `usage_metadata` when round-tripping Event objects to/from Agent Engine, causing `ContextCacheRequestProcessor` to create a new cache on every invocation instead of reusing an existing cache.

The issue provides a repro where in-memory sessions reuse a `cache_name` on the second turn, while Agent Engine sessions create a new cache each turn with a different fingerprint and no `cache_name` reuse.
The reporter claims this has "never worked" with VertexAiSessionService (tested ADK 1.19.0 and 1.25.1).

records.title: Bug: Context becomes full and /compact stops working after using subagents (Task tool) #16209
records.relevance_note: Field failure where subagent/tool output growth can exhaust context and prevent compaction from running, eliminating recovery path.
records.reason_included: Captures a specific stale-context / capacity failure mode: compaction cannot execute when the working set hits 100%, motivating reserved headroom and subagent summarisation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports that using subagents via the Task tool can cause context usage to spike rapidly to ~100% capacity, after which the `/compact` command becomes unresponsive.
The repro describes repeating subagent usage 2–3 times (file reads/greps) until context reaches ~100%, then `/compact` fails or is ignored, forcing the user to start a new session.

records.title: Claude Code hangs indefinitely during context compaction #19567
records.relevance_note: Detailed repro of compaction hang and non-interruptibility (Ctrl+C ineffective), including orphaned process resource usage and large session-file size.
records.reason_included: High-value failure mode for compaction stop conditions/timeouts in terminal agents: compaction can freeze UI and leak resources for many hours.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports Claude Code becomes completely unresponsive when compaction/summarisation triggers on a large context; the terminal freezes and Ctrl+C has no effect.
The report states the Claude process becomes orphaned (PPID=1) and continues running, consuming high CPU and RAM (example: ~277% CPU and ~11.8 GB RAM) for 26+ hours until manually killed.
The issue links the hang to very large session state (example: ~23+ MB session file) and long tool-heavy workflows with multiple tool calls and subagents.
